addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Render and finish the Highland cinematic film on one NVIDIA GPU (e.g. RTX 4090).
#
#   bash projects/highland/products/walkthrough/runpod_render.sh setup          # Python 3.11, bpy 5.0.1, assets, scene checks
#   bash projects/highland/products/walkthrough/runpod_render.sh bench uhd       # one frame per shot, projected hours
#   bash projects/highland/products/walkthrough/runpod_render.sh render uhd 2    # all frames, 2 processes sharing the GPU
#   bash projects/highland/products/walkthrough/runpod_render.sh finish uhd      # grade, titles, score, encode 4K + 1080p, checks
#   bash projects/highland/products/walkthrough/runpod_render.sh all uhd 2       # everything above in order
#
# Profiles: uhd   = 3840 x 1608, 96 samples: 4K master plus a 1080p cut (default);
#           final = native 1920 x 804, 128 samples: 1080p master only.
# Rendering resumes where it stopped; existing frames are skipped.
# DEVICE=CUDA uses CUDA kernels if OptiX is unavailable on the driver.
set -euo pipefail
STAGE=${1:-all}; PROFILE=${2:-uhd}; WORKERS=${3:-2}; DEVICE=${DEVICE:-OPTIX}
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd); cd "$ROOT"
LOG=build/highland-cinema/logs; mkdir -p "$LOG"
# One uv environment from the committed lock. --no-sync: the bpy 5.0.1 wheel mislabels its
# own tag (cp39), so a syncing `uv run` would reinstall bpy under the parallel render workers.
BPY=(uv run --frozen --no-sync python); FIN=("${BPY[@]}")
MASTER=1080; [ "$PROFILE" = uhd ] && MASTER=2160

setup() {
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv

content.text:
Any of the RTX cards on that page will work. The locked bpy 5.0.1 wheel ships native CUDA kernels for Ampere (`sm_86`), Ada (`sm_89`) and Blackwell (`sm_120`), plus OptiX kernels that compile on the pod for any RTX card. So availability, speed and the vCPU count matter more than compatibility.

**My pick: RTX 6000 Ada ($0.99/hr), or L40S ($1.09/hr) if the 6000 won't start.**
- Both are Ada, the same architecture as the 4090 the RunPod notes target, so you get the same kernels and roughly 4090-class Cycles speed.
- 48 GB of VRAM leaves room for 2–3 render workers on one GPU (`render final 3`).
- 16 vCPUs, against the 4090's 8, help where this pipeline is CPU-bound: per-frame scene sync, and the finish step, which took 73 minutes on 4 vCPUs.
- The L40S showed better availability in your screenshot.

**The other options:**
- **RTX 5090 ($1.19/hr):** probably the fastest, and the wheel supports Blackwell. But it's the least proven path, with newer drivers and nothing run on it yet. It's a fine second choice if the Ada cards are taken.
- **RTX A6000 ($0.59/hr) or A5000 ($0.27/hr):** Ampere, roughly half the Cycles speed. Fine for a cheap preview if you don't mind waiting longer; the cost per frame may come out similar.
- **Skip PRO 6000 MIG:** it's a slice of a GPU, so you'd pay a premium for partial performance.

Whichever you choose, the `bench final` step will tell you the real cost before you commit. It renders one frame per shot and prints the projected hours. Multiply by the hourly rate, and stop there if the number's too high. Nothing in this pipeline has run on a GPU yet, including the 4090, so check the bench frames for anything odd too.

Use the same commands as before, with `render final 3` on a 48 GB card. If the pod's driver doesn't offer OptiX, put `DEVICE=CUDA` in front of the commands.

content.text:
That error comes from where you're cloning, not from git. `/workspace` on this pod is a network volume that doesn't allow `chmod`, and git needs it to create its config lock file. The fix is to keep the repo on the pod's local disk and put only `build/` (frames, logs, scene) on the volume, so a render can still resume after a pod restart:

```bash
rm -rf /workspace/blender-models            # the half-made clone from the failed attempts
cd /root
GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models.git
cd blender-models
mkdir -p /workspace/highland-build
ln -s /workspace/highland-build build       # frames and logs live on the volume
W=projects/highland/products/walkthrough
bash $W/runpod_render.sh setup
```

- **Before the `rm`:** run `ls -la /workspace/blender-models` and make sure it only has a `.git` folder, which means it's just the failed clone.
- **Container disk:** the repo plus the uv environment (Python 3.11 and the bpy wheel) need a few GB of local space. If `df -h /root` shows less than about 10 GB free, tell me and we'll move the uv cache to the volume too.
- **If `setup` fails to write `build/`:** some volumes also reject `chmod` on ordinary files. In that case, remove the symlink (`rm build`) and let `build/` sit on local disk. You lose resume across pod restarts, but the render itself is unaffected.

Then carry on with step 2, `bash $W/runpod_render.sh bench final`, and send me the `projected_hours_one_worker` line.

Here's the full sequence for a fresh pod, with both fixes from last time built in: the repo on local disk, and only `build/` on the volume.

**0. One-time on your laptop (WSL): SSH key**

```bash
ls ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub || ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C runpod     # make a key if you don't have one
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub                                        # paste into RunPod → Settings → SSH Public Keys
```

When deploying, tick **SSH terminal access** and expose TCP port 22 in the template. You need the direct TCP connection to copy files back with `scp`. The `ssh.runpod.io` proxy connection doesn't support `scp`.

**1. Connect**

Use the "SSH over exposed TCP" command from the pod's **Connect** dialog:

```bash
ssh root@<POD_IP> -p <PORT> -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

**2. On the pod: tmux first, so nothing dies with your connection**

```bash
command -v tmux || (apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q tmux)
tmux new -s film               # detach: Ctrl-b d   ·   reattach later: tmux attach -t film
```

**3. Inside tmux: clone and set up**

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/uv                               # uv cache off the network volume (chmod fails there)
grep -q UV_CACHE_DIR ~/.bashrc || echo 'export UV_CACHE_DIR=/root/.cache/uv' >> ~/.bashrc

cd /root
GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1 git clone https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models.git   # username + fine-grained token
cd blender-models
mkdir -p /workspace/highland-build && ln -s /workspace/highland-build build   # frames/logs persist on the volume
W=projects/highland/products/walkthrough

bash $W/runpod_render.sh setup            # ≈ 10 min; ends with "Cinema cameras validated: [...]"
bash $W/runpod_render.sh bench final      # send me the BENCH {...} line
```

- **Clone prompt:** git asks for your GitHub username, then a fine-grained token with read access to the repo as the password.
- **Reusing a volume:** if this pod reuses the earlier network volume, `/workspace/highland-build` already holds the assets, so setup skips downloading them.
- **OptiX errors:** if the bench fails on OptiX, run it again as `DEVICE=CUDA bash $W/runpod_render.sh bench final`.

**4. After you've sent me the bench numbers: render and finish**

```bash
bash $W/runpod_render.sh render final 3 && bash $W/runpod_render.sh finish final
```

- **Watch it** from a second tmux window (`Ctrl-b c`): `tail -f build/highland-cinema/logs/render-final-*.log | grep SHOT`, and `nvidia-smi -l 5` for GPU load. Under about 90% busy means try 4 workers.

**5. Copy the results back (run in WSL, not on the pod)**

```bash

scp -P <PORT> -r root@<POD_IP>:/root/blender-models/deliverables/highland-cinema/ \
    ~/Projects/blender-models/build/highland-cinema/runpod/
```

content.text:
You're in window 0, the render, which is correct. The `*` in the status bar marks the current window, and the render is running there.

In tmux, every command starts with `Ctrl-b`: press Ctrl and b together, let go, then press the next key.

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl-b` then `0`, `1`, `2`, `3` | Jump to that window number |
| `Ctrl-b` then `n` / `p` | Next / previous window |
| `Ctrl-b` then `w` | Pick a window from a list (arrow keys, Enter) |
| `Ctrl-b` then `d` | Detach. Everything keeps running; come back with `tmux attach -t film` |

The hard cut at 24.75 s leads from the warm corridor to the dark exterior, and the ending fades to black into the end card. Next I'm running automated QC across all 792 frames for flicker, clipping, and blank frames.

input.command:
cd /home/kato/Projects/blender-models && uv run --no-sync python - <<'EOF'
import subprocess, json, numpy as np
from bmodels.paths import ROOT
mp4 = ROOT/"build/highland-cinema/runpod/highland-cinema/Highland-cinema-1080p.mp4"
W, H = 480, 270
raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-v","error","-i",str(mp4),"-vf",f"scale={W}:{H}","-f","rawvideo","-pix_fmt","gray","-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
fr = np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8).reshape(-1, H, W).astype(np.float32)/255
pic = fr[:, 33:237]                     # 2.39:1 picture area inside the 16:9 frame (scaled)
spec = json.loads((ROOT/"projects/highland/products/walkthrough/cinema.shots.json").read_text())
print("frames decoded:", len(fr))
start = 0
for s in spec["shots"]:
    a, b = start, start+s["frames"]; seg = pic[a:b]; start = b
    m = seg.mean((1, 2))
    d = np.abs(np.diff(m))
    # 8x8 grid flicker: frame-to-frame change of each cell mean, minus the global trend
    g = seg.reshape(len(seg), 8, seg.shape[1]//8, 8, seg.shape[2]//8).mean((2, 4))
    gd = np.abs(np.diff(g, axis=0) - np.diff(m)[:, None, None])
    clip_hi = (seg > .985).mean()*100; clip_lo = (seg < .015).mean()*100
    print(f"{s['id']:16s} mean {m.mean():.3f}  max |Δmean| {d.max()*100:.2f}%  grid-flicker p99 {np.percentile(gd,99)*100:.2f}% max {gd.max()*100:.2f}%  clip hi {clip_hi:.2f}% lo {clip_lo:.2f}%")
end = pic[start:]
print("end card frames:", len(end), "| black frames in picture section (mean<0.01):", int((pic[:start].mean((1,2)) < .01).sum()))
EOF

for name, at in (('01-title', 3.0), ('02-entry', 6.4), ('03-lobby', 9.0), ('04-slats', 11.6), ('06-elevator', 17.6), ('07-section', 20.3), ('08-corridor-208', 23.2), ('09-release', 27.5)):

    tiles = []
    for s in SPEC['shots']:
        at = starts[s['id']]+s['frames']/FPS*.6
        tile = build/f'tile-{s["id"]}.png'
        subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-y', '-v', 'error', '-ss', f'{at:.3f}', '-i', str(lossless), '-frames:v', '1', '-vf', f'crop={PW}:{PH}:0:{TOP},scale=640:-2', str(tile)], check=True)

    rows = (len(tiles)+1)//2  # two tiles per row; sized from the shot list, not a fixed edit
    sheet = Image.new('RGB', (1280, rows*(268+34)), (8, 8, 8)); d = ImageDraw.Draw(sheet)
    for k, (s, at, im) in enumerate(tiles):
        x, y = (k % 2)*640, (k//2)*(268+34)
        sheet.paste(im, (x, y+34)); tracked(d, (x+10, y+9), f'{s["id"].upper()}   {at:05.2f} S', font('NotoSans-Regular.ttf', 15), GOLD, 2)

input.new_string:
Never put it on rotation, because Rule 1 locks the camera level.
- **Unwrap yaw when keying cameras from `atan2`** (found on the Highland film, 2026-11-08). A camera looking
  along −x sits on the ±π seam, so a few mm of drift flips the key from +90° to −270°. That's the same
  direction, but Blender interpolates Euler keys, so inside the motion-blur shutter the camera spins 360°.
  The result is two washed-out, ghosted frames that a quaternion-based "rotation step" check reports as 0°.
  Keep yaw continuous (`yaw += 2π·round((prev−yaw)/2π)`), and validate the Euler key steps themselves, not
  only the quaternion difference. Wider lesson: run the automated flicker check (8.8) on the finished film;
  the 3-frames-per-shot diagnostics missed this.
- **Exterior camera distance is limited by the site.** At 2.39:1 a 24 mm lens frames less height than at 16:9.
  On a narrow street you can't back up across it (the Highland camera ended up inside the OSM massing
  opposite, which validation caught), so gain distance along the street with an oblique view instead.

Highland cinema: fix the shot 06 yaw-wrap ghost; shot sheet shows all shots

Review of the first GPU preview (RunPod RTX 6000 Ada, final profile, all finish
checks passing) found two problems:

- Film frames 447-448 (shot 06, native 348-349) were washed out and ghosted.
  The camera looks along -x, where atan2 wraps; the drift flipped the yaw key
  from +90 to -270 deg, and Euler interpolation spun the camera a full turn
  inside the motion-blur shutter. camera() now keeps yaw continuous, and
  validate() fails any Euler key step over 1.5 deg (the quaternion check sees
  the wrap as 0 deg). Re-rendered locally: frames 67-71 are clean.
- The shot sheet canvas was fixed at 4 rows, so shot 09 fell off the bottom;
  it is now sized from the shot list.

Skill: camera notes on the yaw wrap and on exterior distance limits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin highland/cinema-yaw-wrap-fix 2>&1 | tail -1; gh pr create --base main --title "Highland cinema: fix the shot 06 yaw-wrap ghost; shot sheet shows all shots" -F - <<'EOF'
Fixes the two problems found reviewing the first GPU preview of the film. It was rendered on a RunPod RTX 6000 Ada with the `final` profile: 702 frames in about 31 min, and every finish check passed.

## Changes
- **Ghosted frames in shot 06 (film frames 447–448).**
  - **Cause:** the camera looks along −x, where `atan2` wraps from +π to −π. The few millimetres of handheld drift flipped the yaw key from +90° to −270°. That's the same direction, but Blender interpolates Euler keys, so inside the motion-blur shutter the camera spun a full turn and smeared two frames.
  - **Why nothing caught it:** camera validation measures rotation steps as quaternions, which see the wrap as 0°.
  - **Fix:** `camera()` now keeps yaw continuous, and `validate()` also fails any Euler key step over 1.5°. Re-rendered locally, frames 67–71 are clean, with brightness going 113.9 → 115.8 instead of jumping to 140. The largest Euler step anywhere in the film is now 0.26°.
- **Shot sheet missing shot 09.** The canvas was fixed at 4 rows, so the 9th tile fell off the bottom. It's now sized from the shot list.
- **Skill:** the camera section gains two lessons: the yaw-wrap trap, and that the site limits how far an exterior camera can back up.

## Review of the rest of the preview
- Automated QC on all 792 frames:
  - Brightness changes under 0.5% per frame within shots everywhere except shot 06, the bug above.
  - No highlight clipping.
  - The only black frames are the 4 fade-in frames.
- The dusk exteriors (01, 09) have 8–11% near-black pixels, from the vignette and night shadows. I looked at them and they read as intended.

## Verification
- `bm check --base origin/main` and `bm run highland/walkthrough check` pass. The ruff findings are the same 5 that are on `main`.
- Camera validation passes for all 9 shots with the new Euler check.

## Note for the next GPU run
The scene code changed, so `cinema.py` sets the earlier frames aside as stale and re-renders all 702. That's about 31 min on the same pod.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
